title: A child in the middle (Mark 9:30–50)
hookLine: they argue who's greatest; he puts a child among them

lines: HE'LL BE KILLED. THEY'RE AFRAID TO ASK.
cards: The drive home when the kids in the back seat have been fighting, and the second you ask what's going on, it goes silent. That's today.
Walking through Galilee, Jesus tells his disciples a second time that he'll be handed over and killed and rise again. Mark says they didn't understand, and they were afraid to ask.
So they talked about something else, just out of his hearing. Home in Capernaum, he asks what they were arguing about on the road. Nobody says a word.

teach.b: First, the argument: which of them was the greatest. Right after he told them he was going to die. It's almost funny, and very human.
Second, he sits down. In that world a teacher sat to teach, so Mark is saying: this is the lesson.

teach.h: LAST OF ALL, SERVANT OF ALL.
teach.b: He calls the twelve and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "If any man desire to be first, he shall be the last of all, and the minister of all." The Greek for minister is diakonos, a servant, the one who waits on tables.
It's where the Church gets the word deacon. Third, the child.

teach.h: A CHILD IN THE MIDDLE, EMBRACED.
teach.b: He stands a little child in the middle of them, then wraps his arms around the child. In his world a child had no status: no rights, no say, nobody's idea of great.

And he says: "Whosoever shall receive one such child as this in my name, receiveth me." Welcome the one who can't do anything for you, and you've welcomed him. Fourth, the rest of the chapter turns the same idea.

teach.h: NOT AGAINST YOU IS FOR YOU.
teach.b: John complains that a stranger is driving out demons in Jesus's name, and Jesus says let him be: "he that is not against you, is for you." Even a cup of water given in his name won't lose its reward.
The chapter ends: have peace among you. Look back at this week in Mark: crumbs under the table, the baskets, men as trees, who do you say I am, the mountain, a father's cry.

teach.h: WHOSOEVER SHALL RECEIVE ONE SUCH CHILD.
teach.b: And now a child in the middle, where the greatest one should be.

how: In the Catholic Church the diaconate takes its name from this servant word, and the Pope's traditional title, Servant of the Servants of God, echoes the same teaching about being last of all.

o: a servant, the one who waits on tables
a priest who offers the Temple sacrifice
a scribe who copies and teaches the Law

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: a servant; where deacon comes from
not against you is for you

s: the disciples argued about greatness right after he spoke of his death
Mark places the argument on the road, right after the second prediction.
in Jesus's world, children were honored as the most important people
a child had almost no status, which is why the gesture was so striking.
the word deacon comes from the Greek for servant
diakonos, the one who waits on tables.

games.q: you're one of the twelve. he asks what you were arguing about on the road, and it was which of you is greatest. what do you do?
o: explain that it was a fair question.
games.why: they held their peace. then he sat down, called them, and set a child in the middle.

practice: Picture tomorrow's small doors, a line at the store, a merge in traffic, the last slice, who talks first at dinner, and choose one where you'll quietly step back and let someone else be first.
Then picture the person with the least say in your day, maybe a child, maybe someone older, maybe someone everyone overlooks, and imagine putting them in the middle. If you pray, hold them there.

wordCard.voice: Diakonos. The Greek word for minister Jesus uses after sitting the twelve down: a servant, the one who waits on tables, where the Church gets the word deacon. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: last of all. the verse goes on, servant of all, diakonos.

carryVoice: Your line: last of all. Servant of all comes right after it. That's a week in Mark, and day two hundred seventeen.
